corroboration.canonicalColoursIntactInTheseChapters: every canonical role that IS rendered in the five chapters shows its correct token colour — e.g. b2-34 verb 118/118 rgb(220,38,38), subject 71/71 rgb(24,95,165), negation 2/2 rgb(192,38,211); c1-08 preposition 196/196 rgb(202,138,4); b2-65 modalverb 2/2 rgb(159,18,57)
corroboration.p15Agreement: none of the five chapters has any HEADWORD_COLOUR_MISMATCH finding in P15, which is exactly what zero affected tokens predicts
corroboration.note: two unrelated colour populations were observed and are NOT collisions: object/conjunction/name spans at rgb(90,90,96) (ink-secondary, the documented ROLE_COLOR_VAR mapping) and article spans at rgb(22,58,55) inside vocabulary chips (the .vword-de .art override in the same local block)

hiddenCollisionCheck.note: single-role block; no other canonical name
both already in scope; r-cause/topic/means/benefit/authority are non-canonical
a SECOND local rule .r-subjective {color: rgb(192,57,43)} exists; r-subjective is NOT canonical — no collision
.r-adjektiv and .r-nomen are German-spelled near-misses of canonical .r-adjective / .r-nnoun — they do NOT collide today, but they show how close the naming convention runs to the canonical namespace

recommendationForPhase21.scope: apply the minimal fix to the 5 PROVEN chapters only (c1-01 .r-verb, c1-02 .r-time, c1-05 .r-negation, c1-07 .r-genitiv, c1-17 .r-modalverb) — 5 selector edits, 73 learner-visible occurrences restored
recommendationForPhase21.theseSix: leave the six Class-B collisions in place OR clean them opportunistically; they are latent, not harmful. Cleaning them is cheap and removes a trap for future authoring, but it changes no rendered pixel today and carries a small risk of touching a chapter that needs no change.
recommendationForPhase21.guard: the stronger value is the lint rule from P19 option 4 — these six prove the collision pattern recurs across levels (B2 and C1) and is one bad name away from becoming visible
recommendationForPhase21.verification: after any edit, re-render only the touched chapters and confirm the affected role reports its canonical token colour; a full sweep is not required to prove a colour change

constraints: no production file, chapter data, CSS, QA engine, assertion, lint rule or baseline modified
